changelog:
Two faults the adverts turned up the moment they ran on a real server, both of them about a break no longer being one airing.

A channel reported an advert that had already finished. A window begins at the airing covering its first moment, and a break is now rebuilt into several - adverts, then the trailer, then what is left - so the first entry the schedule hands back is not necessarily the thing that is on. What is on air is now the entry that covers this moment, and anything already over is dropped before the guide is drawn.

A break could fill with adverts and leave the trailer nowhere to go. Room is reserved for the trailer before any advert is placed, but the reservation was measured from local trailer *files* - and nearly every trailer a library has is a link the client resolves, whose length the server never learns. That measured zero, so with a pool of any size the adverts would take the whole break. A linked trailer now reserves two and a half minutes; over-reserving costs a little quiet at the end of a break, which is what a break was before any of this.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
